Author: Nagesh Bheemapaka
Bench: Nagesh Bheemapaka
 The Honourable Sri Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka
 Writ Petition No.14617 of 2025
Order:

Petitioner claims to be the absolute owner and possessor of land admeasuring Ac.0.30 gts in Survey No.451/1 of Yadgiripalli Village, Miryalaguda Mandal, Nalgonda District, said to have been inherited through a notarized Will dated 31.10.2019 executed by late Smt.Gade Yashodamma.

Petitioner alleges illegal encroachment by the officials of the Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (TGSPDCL), who have allegedly commenced construction of a 33/11 KV Electric Substation on the petitioner's land, despite the existence of a mutation and issuance of a Pattadar Passbook in his name.

entities.text: Telangana State Southern Power Distribution Company Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Bonkuri Sridhar, learned counsel for petitioner and Sri N.Sreedhar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel for TGSPDCL, for respondent Nos.2 to 5.
Perused the record.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that the main grievance of the petitioner is that the officials of TGSPDCL, in collusion with the revenue authorities, have trespassed into his private land and dispossessed him without due process, in NBK, J wp_14617_2025 violation of Articles 14, 21,
and 300-A of the Constitution of India.

He further contended that petitioner was in lawful possession of the subject land, and despite having brought the issue to the notice of the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) and other authorities through multiple representations and under the RTI Act, no remedial action was taken.
He further submits that the construction is being carried out without acquisition, compensation, or following any lawful procedure.
Therefore, prayed this Court to direct the respondent No.5 to vacate the suit Schedule property and restore possession to the petitioner.
4. Learned Standing Counsel for the TGSPDCL, appearing for respondent Nos. 2 to 5, filed a counter affidavit stating that there is no encroachment upon the petitioner's land.
It is stated that based on the request of TGSPDCL, the District Collector, Nalgonda, allotted land admeasuring 0.22 acres in Survey No. 451/2, and possession was handed over to TGSPDCL on 07.03.2022.
The construction is being undertaken in the said Government land and not in Survey No. 451/1 as alleged by the petitioner.
It is contended that there appears to be some confusion on the part of the petitioner in identification of the NBK, J wp_14617_2025 property.
It is further contended that the land was identified by the Revenue Department prior to such allotment and that the survey numbers are distinct.

sentences.text: Upon consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the record, it is evident that the dispute essentially pertains to identification of boundaries and alleged encroachment, which involves disputed questions of fact that cannot be adjudicated in exercise of writ jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

It is a settled principle of law that when the adjudication of rights requires examination of complex and disputed facts, including land boundaries, title, and possession, the appropriate remedy lies before the competent civil court.
6.
Accordingly the writ petition is dismissed.
However, the petitioner, if so advised, is at liberty to approach the civil court for appropriate relief.
There shall be no other as to costs.
